title: A Funny Film About Manhole Covers Wins a Big Prize
summary:
A comedy about two people who steal manhole covers has won the top prize at the Tokyo International Film Festival.

The film is called "Sister Brother Manhole Cover." It tells the story of Viktor and Malina, a brother and sister who make money by stealing manhole covers and copper statues. Their adventure gets wild when a stolen bronze statue of a national hero falls on Viktor's foot.

The prize is worth 3 million yen, about $19,000. The festival's jury leader, Rolf de Heer, said the jury picked the film because it is both touching and playful, and shows humanity and compassion toward its characters.

The director, Milcho Manchevski, could not be in Tokyo, so the film's producer and its two stars accepted the prize. "We came here to Tokyo with a manhole cover, and we are going back to Macedonia with a beautiful award," said producer Jane Kortoshev.

Another prize, the Special Jury Prize, went to "Magic Atlas," an animated film from Singapore that its artist spent about ten years making.
why_it_matters: It proves a small, funny film from a faraway country can beat big productions — a good reminder that your own silly ideas can go far.
